title: Parity-selective spin splitting in coplanar antiferromagnets via bichromatic driving
authors: Di Zhu, Zhongbo Yan, Mohsen Yarmohammadi
abstract: Parity is a central characteristic of momentum-dependent spin splitting in antiferromagnets (AFMs). Yet, intrinsic crystal symmetries typically restrict the splitting to either even or odd parity, preventing flexible spin control. Using a coplanar AFM, we demonstrate that bichromatic ($ω$--$nω$) Floquet driving offers a natural way to bypass this constraint. This mechanism generates asymmetric spin textures unattainable in static AFMs or under monochromatic driving. For the specific AFM considered here, we reveal an elegant relation between spin-splitting parity and harmonic hierarchy: $ω$--$2ω$ fields generate highly tunable odd- and mixed-parity spin splittings, whereas higher-order harmonics ($n \ge 3$) exclusively produce even-parity states. The macroscopic magnetization can also be toggled via the specific driving protocol and harmonic $n$. These distinct spin splitting states manifest in qualitatively different macroscopic spin currents generated after an optical quench---a definitive transport signature complementing direct visualization via spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
summary: The paper demonstrates that applying bichromatic light fields ($\omega - n\omega$) to a coplanar antiferromagnet allows researchers to overcome inherent crystal symmetry restrictions on spin-splitting parity. By tuning the driving frequency ratio ($n$), one can deterministically generate odd, mixed, or even spin textures, which are confirmed by measurable transport signatures like quench-induced spin currents.
main_problem: The primary challenge is overcoming the intrinsic crystal symmetry limitations that restrict spin-splitting parity in antiferromagnets (AFMs) to only even or odd values.
main_result: Bichromatic Floquet driving ($\omega - n\omega$) provides a mechanism to deterministically control the spin-splitting parity, generating tunable odd-, mixed-, and even-parity states impossible with static or monochromatic fields.
method: The analysis uses Floquet theory applied to a tight-binding Hamiltonian under bichromatic time-dependent potentials, deriving an effective time-independent Hamiltonian in the high-frequency limit.
model_or_system: The system is a coplanar Antiferromagnet (BCAFM) realized in engineered 2D heterostructures. The physics is modeled using a tight-binding Hamiltonian subjected to bichromatic driving fields ($\omega - n\omega$).
key_observables: Spin-splitting parity (Odd, Even, Mixed), macroscopic spin currents ($J_{s x}, J_{s y}$), and momentum-resolved spin polarization measured via ARPES.
important_parameters: The harmonic number $n$ of the driving field, and the relative amplitudes/polarizations of the two driving frequencies ($\omega$ and $2\omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the high-frequency off-resonant Floquet approximation, truncating the Hamiltonian expansion at specific orders in $\omega^{-1}$ or $\omega^{-2}$.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate momentum-resolved spin polarization ($\langle s_z angle$) for different driving protocols (BLPL, BCPL, BCLPL) and harmonics ($n=2$), showing distinct parity outcomes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the effective Floquet Hamiltonian by expanding the time-dependent lattice Hamiltonian using Peierls substitution. It then analyzes this effective Hamiltonian for various bichromatic polarization states (BLPL, BCPL, BCLPL) to map out the resulting spin-splitting parity based on the harmonic number $n$.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses how external time-periodic driving fields can be used as a quantum control knob to engineer fundamental symmetries and electronic properties in condensed matter systems, which is highly relevant for topological materials and spintronics.
